title: Protocol marshaller: map OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 <-> Redwood request/response
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a production-safe marshaller that translates OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions) requests and streaming responses into Redwood's internal request/response model and back. The goal is to support 1) non-streamed responses, 2) chunked streaming (delta tokens + function_call fragments), 3) function/tool calling semantics, and 4) structured output paths (JSON schema enforcement). This ticket covers the spec, transform code, unit/integration tests, and a rollout plan behind a feature flag. Key constraints: preserve stable semantics for role/system/user/message ordering, exact stop-sequence handling, deterministic function_call argument assembly when streamed, and conservative error mappings to OpenAI-style error codes for client compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI-style POST /v1/chat/completions maps to Redwood internal Generate request with message list, temperature/top_p, n, max_tokens, stop[] and function hints preserved.
Non-streaming responses return valid OpenAI-compatible JSON body with choices[].message, finish_reason and usage fields computed from Redwood cost accounting.

Streaming mode (stream=true) emits SSE-style 'data: [DELTA]' events matching OpenAI convention: initial 'data: [DONE]' behavior and incremental content/delta events including partial function_call.name and function_call.arguments fragments assembled on receiver side.

Function/tool call requests from models are converted to Redwood ToolCall messages with a stable id; when streamed, partial argument fragments reassembled into valid JSON or a safe fallback error when invalid after timeout.

Structured output support: when model emits JSON or uses tool schema, Redwood validates against provided JSON schema; validation failures produce a mapped OpenAI 'invalid_response' style error and a developer-friendly message in the console/console-logs.
Comprehensive unit tests covering role permutations, stop sequence edge cases (multi-token stops), and timeboxed partial function argument assembly under stream backpressure.
Integration test against a forked model runtime that simulates interleaved assistant content and function_call deltas; expected choice stream matches OpenAI shape.
Rollout disabled by default and gated behind runtime-compatibility feature flag; canary to 5% traffic with metric dashboards for correctness and latency.
Documentation PR with mapping table and examples (requests + streaming events) merged before flag removal.
Security review completed for any parsing or object-merge logic that could allow injection via streamed fragments.
comments: 2026-02-14: Spike done — prototype translator live in local dev: https://go/repo/pr/4582 (draft). Observations: stop sequences relying on token boundaries required token-aware scanning; naive substring match breaks cases where tokenizer splits stop tokens.

2026-02-20: Design review with PM/Design. Decided to represent function_call fragments with three event types: fc.start (with name), fc.args (raw fragment), fc.end (signal). This trades stricter ordering for easier client consumption. Action: add fc.* events to SSE mapping and implement assembly buffer with max 5s merge window.
2026-02-25: UX/Console note — we'll surface partial function call previews in the Console's request inspector. Linking design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/compat-marshaller-design

2026-03-02: Found an edge where multiple choices (n>1) with streaming interleave cause ambiguous association of function_call fragments to choice index. Decided: attach fc events to choice index field in SSE event; update spec and tests.

2026-03-09: Security review request submitted (SEC-REQ-789). Focus: streamed JSON reassembly, memory bounds, and injection risk. SEC feedback: require a strict max argument size (256KB) and defensive JSON parse with SAX-style validation. Implementing as part of this ticket.
implementation_notes:
Transforms are implemented as a thin marshalling layer in the public ingress service. Key modules:
- request_parser: normalize incoming OpenAI fields -> Redwood message schema (preserve role order; system messages first).
- response_emitter: map Redwood deltas to OpenAI SSE frames. Emit explicit control events: 'fc.start','fc.args','fc.end' plus text_delta events to avoid ambiguous token attribution.
- function_assembler: stream-safe buffer that concatenates fc.args, validates JSON schema, and emits a single tool invocation to the runtime. Timeouts: if assembly does not complete within 5s (canary) or exceeds 256KB, produce a mapped error to client and record detailed console log for support.
- stop-handler: token-aware stop detection. Uses tokenizer from runtime to respect split tokens; fallback heuristic for unknown tokenizers: longest-prefix match with byte-level boundaries.

Performance: adding marshalling should add <3ms median overhead; streaming path optimized to avoid full-message copies by using zero-copy slices where possible.
test_plan: Unit tests for request_parser and response_emitter. End-to-end integration tests with simulated streaming model that emits content and function fragments in interleaved order. Load test in staging with 1000 concurrent streaming sessions to validate memory caps and backpressure handling. Canary: route 5% of existing openai-compat traffic for one week, monitor correctness, 95th percentile latency change, error rate increase.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge with feature flag off. 2) Internal dogfood for 48h. 3) Canary 5% for 7 days. 4) Expand to 25% if metrics stable. 5) Remove flag after 30 days and documentation updates.
notes_for_support: When customers report broken streaming reconstruction: ask for raw SSE transcript (data: lines), the request payload (messages + functions), and the generated function_call fragments. Check console logs for 'fc-assembly-timeout' or 'fc-assembly-size-limit' tags. Use replay harness at https://qa.playback/compat to reproduce.
